We fund, install and operate batteries on-site at small businesses, then supply their power at a firm, flat rate 20–40% below incumbents, making the economics work by optimising those batteries against wholesale prices. We're live with real customers. Team of six, backed by Systemiq and Black Nova; engineering includes Casey, who previously led Google engineering in Paris and Google Maps in Sydney. We're AI-native: engineers, energy specialists and go-to-market colleagues all ship with coding agents. Each engineer owns a product end to end, from the commercial problem through to production. Flat structure, lots of ownership. Areas you could own: * Customer experience: quoting, onboarding and the customer app * Metering and billing: turning high-volume interval data into accurate bills * Energy-market and battery data: the market, weather and telemetry pipelines behind our decisions * The agent-driven development platform the whole team builds on Stack: TypeScript, React, Postgres, serverless. Intro chat, system design, an agentic build, then a day with the team. Apply at https://jobs.cable.energy/roles/3e2cd174-71f5-80ae-a1d2-db8b... or email theo@cable.energy.

Understanding demand charges | Cable Energy Skip to content Login Get a quote Menu Guide Understanding demand charges: why timing changes your bill Written by César Smet Published 2 October 2026 4 min read On this page The ovens are on, the dishwasher starts and the air conditioning is working hard. For half an hour, your business needs a lot of power at once. On some electricity tariffs, a busy period like that can affect more than the electricity you use that afternoon. It can help set a separate charge on your bill: a demand charge . What is a demand charge? A usage charge is based on how much electricity you use. A demand charge is based on a measure of how much power you draw from the grid at once. The network has to be able to deliver electricity during busy periods. Demand pricing is one way it charges for that capacity. Your retailer decides how those costs appear in your electricity offer. Not every offer has a separate demand charge. kW and kWh, in two lines kWh is the amount of electricity used , like the distance travelled on a road trip. kW is how quickly it’s being used , like your speed.
